body:
Good morning, Bakersfield. It’s Saturday, August 22, 2026 — a day that’s already bringing difficult news, as a 15-year-old has been arrested in connection with a deadly shooting at Independence High School. We’re seeing a high near 100° today, with air quality at a moderate 58. Let’s take a look at what happened overnight, what’s making news, and what’s coming up this week.

## The Kern Overnight

The night’s most serious call came just after midnight, when a witness reported seeing someone shot at a Taco Bell in the Baker Street area. The suspect — described as a white male in his 40s to 50s, wearing a black shirt and dark pants — was last seen sitting inside a white vehicle, possibly a Ford Explorer. Officers responded with an officer-safety broadcast. Before that, crews knocked down a fire at a vacant house on King Street around 2:16 a.m., where flames were visible inside a single-story structure with heavy smoke showing. Multiple engines and a truck company responded, and the fire was under control by about 2:25. Earlier in the evening, just before 11 p.m., a two-vehicle collision left one vehicle on fire near Gosford Road and Harris Road. Engine 14 and Engine 9 responded to what command dubbed the Harris Incident, though injuries were unknown. A reported grass fire along southbound Highway 395 north of Brown Road drew a heavy response around 10:15 p.m., with engines, patrol units, a water tender, a dozer and a helicopter dispatched. Crews found a small roadside fire that was quickly extinguished, and the extra equipment was canceled. Elsewhere, an assault with a knife was reported around 10:38 p.m., though no injuries were reported. The suspect — about 6 feet tall with neck tattoos, wearing black shorts, a gray shirt and white shoes — fled on foot northbound. Overnight also saw a subject reported with a firearm in his waistband on Houchin Road around 10:04 p.m., an assault reported on Birch Avenue in Wasco around 11:22 p.m., a hit-and-run on Monterey Street involving a black Camry and a white sedan around 11:23 p.m., two fire hydrants reported spilling water on 22nd Street between Q and P streets around 11:53 p.m., about a half acre burning behind a residence on Windsong Street around 12:01 a.m., a suspicious vehicle check on Culiacan Avenue around 12:09 a.m., a family disturbance on Suncrest Drive involving an intoxicated teenager around 12:10 a.m., and a welfare check on a man lying on the ground near the curb on 26th Street around 12:12 a.m.

## Today's weather

We’re in for a hot one today, with a high near 100° and a low around 74° tonight. It’s currently 95° at Meadows Field (KBFL), and there are no active weather alerts for Kern County. Air quality is holding at a moderate 58 — no fires are actively burning in the county at this time.

## Top stories

**KGET 17 reports that a 15-year-old has been arrested in connection with a deadly shooting at Independence High School.** The arrest came Saturday morning in the 7500 block of Stockdale Highway, according to Bakersfield Police. The incident took place during a football game between Independence and Centennial High Schools on Friday evening. No other arrests have been announced, and no other suspects have been identified at this time. The investigation is ongoing. This story is developing, and details will be updated as they become available.

**23ABC tells us the Kern County Sheriff's Office has merged emergency units to speed up water rescues.** Sergeant Rodney Jones with the Kern County Sheriff's Office said that while deputies can warn residents about the dangers of rivers and lakes, those warnings have limits. "If they're in the proper safety gear - a helmet, a life-vest, and they can swim - I can't stop them from doing that." Since the day after Memorial Day, the sheriff's office has recorded eight rescues and five recovered persons from the Lower and Upper Kern River. A two-day training session at Pyles Boys Camp near Lake Ming gave volunteers hands-on practice in critical search and rescue tactics. Kern County Sheriff's Office Public Information Officer Lori Meza said combining water and aerial support gives rescuers multiple vantage points to more precisely locate someone in danger. "You know that seconds make the difference...like I said...merging these skills from not only being able to hike to where the location is but also to be able to see where their location is..." Meza said the goal is not only to save lives, but also to teach the public what signs to watch for when someone may be in danger.

**KGET 17 says that if you're worried about flesh-eating bacteria, there are warning signs to watch for.** With summer in full swing and many people enjoying outdoor activities, it's important to know the symptoms of this rare but serious infection. The station advises watching for redness, swelling, or warmth around a wound, as well as fever and chills. If you experience any of these symptoms after spending time in natural bodies of water, it's best to seek medical attention immediately. This story is part of KGET's ongoing coverage of health and safety issues in Kern County.

## Something good

In a move that’s expected to enhance response times and improve safety for residents during water-related emergencies, the Kern County Sheriff's Office has merged emergency units to speed up water rescues. This proactive step comes as summer activities continue, and it’s a reminder of the department’s commitment to keeping our community safe.

## Coming up this week

If you’re looking for something to do, the Fox Theater has a full lineup of events this week. Tonight, Saturday, August 22, you can catch Los Yonic's Zamacona, Los caminantes, y Grupo Yndio. On Tuesday, August 25, the theater will host Cults & Classics: Season Pass 2026-2027. Later in the week, Rodney Carrington takes the stage on Thursday, August 27, followed by CUMBIATRON: THE CUMBIA RAVE on Friday, August 28. Willie Barcena performs on Saturday, August 29, and that same evening, you can enjoy Michael Return Of The King Tribute Featuring Michael Phoenix. 

For those interested in local government, the Bakersfield City Council has several meetings scheduled for Wednesday, August 26. A Special City Council Meeting will take place at 12:00 p.m., followed by City Council Meeting 330 at 3:30 p.m. and City Council Meeting 515 at 5:15 p.m. These meetings are open to the public, and residents are encouraged to attend and participate in local decision-making.
